exposure: subcutaneous saline irrigation during closure of emergency Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS) incision
outcome: postoperative surgical site complications (seroma, hematoma, superficial surgical site infection)
cohort: The study included 100 women who underwent emergency Lower Segment Caesarean Sections (LSCS).
finding: Subcutaneous saline irrigation during emergency LSCS incision closure significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative surgical site complications, including seroma (8% vs 18%), hematoma (6% vs 20%), and superficial surgical site infections (4% vs 24%).
